title: AI Diagrams Are Ugly. This Free Skill Fixes Them
description:
AI diagrams usually come out as spaghetti: boxes everywhere, arrows crossing arrows, five colours at once. Diagram Design is a free, open-source skill for AI coding agents that draws them the way a design studio would, and it has over 49,000 GitHub stars.

How it works
• Install it once (npx skills add cathrynlavery/diagram-design), then ask your agent: "draw an architecture diagram of my app".
• The agent picks one of 44 diagram types, tells you its plan, and writes a single self-contained HTML + SVG file: no build step, no JavaScript.
• The trick is restraint: one accent colour for the one thing that matters, 1px hairline borders, no shadows, and every coordinate on a 4px grid. In its README's words: "The highest-quality move is usually deletion."

What else it does
• 44 types, from architecture, flowcharts and timelines to Sankeys, Wardley maps and exploded axonometric views.
• Redraws old draw.io, Mermaid and Excalidraw files, with a ledger of what it merged, collapsed or dropped.
• Brand onboarding: give it your website and it pulls your palette and fonts, and checks text contrast (WCAG AA).
• Works with Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot, Cursor and other agent-skill hosts; exports SVG or PNG.

The catch
Output quality depends on the model, the same prompt can lay out differently between runs, and you get a finished picture, not an editable canvas. For diagrams that live in Git and change often, the README itself says Mermaid is the better fit.
